extracted.intended_audience: NOAA B-WET project staff, educators, and communications leads (grantees/partners)
extracted.subtask_short: writing social media posts for B-WET
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and ready-to-use sample content for creating Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram posts to promote NOAA B-WET projects. Includes practical tips (photos, tagging, hashtags), recommended NOAA accounts, and adaptable sample copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use photos with posts
rubrics_metrics.description: It is always better to include a photo (or more) with your post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including photos makes posts more engaging; sample posts assume photos accompany the copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include project/activity location
rubrics_metrics.description: Include where your project/activity takes place. You can even hashtag (#) the particular city/town you are in!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing location information helps local engagement and makes content more relevant; consider hashtagging the city/town.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adapt sample posts as templates
rubrics_metrics.description: The document contains sample posts can be used either “as is” or as templates for customized material to share on Facebook, Twitter, or Instagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feel free to update or remove placeholders for specific project information, or treat the sample posts as general guidelines in developing your own content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include link to project launch press release or webpage
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample posts include a placeholder for [link to local project launch press release or webpage].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linking to a press release or project webpage directs interested readers to more information and supports local publicity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe Twitter character limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Twitter (280-character count): sample tweets are written to fit within Twitter's 280-character limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep copy concise for Twitter and consider using photos/tags judiciously; tag @NOAAeducation in Twitter photos to avoid using characters in the tweet body.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag specific pages/people/groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag a specific page/person/group when you can.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging relevant organizations or individuals increases visibility and the chance of reposting or engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag NOAA accounts appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: NOAA has various accounts on Facebook, Twitter, and Instagram. Tagging these NOAA accounts in your posts, as appropriate, may result in more re-posting and sharing of your content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tagging the NOAA B-WET and NOAA Education pages helps ensure that their social media contributors see and can share your content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preferred NOAA handles to tag
rubrics_metrics.description: Below is a list of relevant NOAA social media accounts; however, it is best to tag @NOAABWET on Facebook and @NOAAeducation on Twitter and Instagram.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed accounts: NOAA Bay Watershed Education and Training — Facebook: @NOAABWET; NOAA Education — Facebook: @NOAAeducation, Twitter: @NOAAeducation, Instagram: @NOAAeducation; NOAA — Facebook: @NOAA, Twitter: @NOAA, Instagram: @NOAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the primary hashtag #NOAABWET
rubrics_metrics.description: Please use the primary hashtag of #NOAABWET whenever possible in adapting sample posts or developing original content to join the broader social conversation with and about the B-WET program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the primary hashtag connects your posts to the broader program conversation and increases discoverability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include additional recommended hashtags
rubrics_metrics.description: Additional hashtags you might consider include: #healthywatersheds #watersheded #learnoutdoors #STEM #environment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these topic hashtags to connect your content to relevant subject-area conversations and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link Facebook posts on Twitter via timestamp URL
rubrics_metrics.description: You can link to a specific Facebook post on Twitter by clicking on the specific Facebook post’s timestamp and copying that URL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This preserves the Facebook content context and allows cross-platform linking between Twitter and Facebook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tag @NOAAeducation in Twitter photos to save characters
rubrics_metrics.description: Tag @NOAAeducation in Twitter photos so that you do not use up your 280 characters on NOAA Education’s Twitter handle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adding the handle as a photo tag keeps the tweet text shorter while still notifying NOAA.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use explicit examples for framing messages
rubrics_metrics.description: Sample content provides concrete tweet and Facebook post phrasing (e.g., 'Students in [local area] will use their watershed as an out-of-school classroom to build #STEM skills. #NOAABWET @NOAAeducation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these examples as inspiration for tone, length, and structure when crafting your own posts; replace placeholders (e.g., [local area], [link], [School/district/project]) with local details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aim for broad audience appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: The sample content in this toolkit supports social media promotion of your B-WET project and is designed to appeal to a broad audience, with options for Facebook and Twitter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Craft messaging that is accessible to non-specialists while highlighting program impact and student engagement.
